guidance.title: One-week movement guide
guidance.safety: This is a general example, not a prescription. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or chest discomfort, and ask a qualified healthcare professional before starting if you have a medical condition, are pregnant, are older, or have been inactive for a long time.
guidance.source: General pattern: WHO 2020 physical activity guidance and CDC 2018 Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans. Source checked 24 November 2026.

muscleGain.title: Underweight or slim: muscle-building focus
muscleGain.summary: The aim is steady, progressive strength work with enough rest. Add difficulty only when you can finish the week without pain.
muscleGain.monday: Full-body strength: squat or chair rise, push-up variation, row, hip hinge and plank; 2 easy sets of 8–12 reps.
muscleGain.tuesday: 20–30 minute easy walk and 5 minutes of mobility.
muscleGain.wednesday: Full-body strength: step-up, shoulder press, band row, deadlift pattern and side plank; 2 sets of 8–12.
muscleGain.thursday: Rest or gentle stretch for 15 minutes.
muscleGain.friday: Repeat Monday with one extra rep or slightly heavier resistance if comfortable.
muscleGain.saturday: 20–40 minute low-effort walk or cycle; finish with calf and hip stretches.
muscleGain.sunday: Complete rest. If you feel pain, stop and ask a professional before continuing.

athleticMaintenance.title: Healthy range, athletic build: maintain and train
athleticMaintenance.summary: BMI can overstate body fat in muscular people. Use performance, waist measurement and how you feel alongside BMI.
athleticMaintenance.monday: Lower-body strength: squat, lunge, Romanian deadlift and calf raise; 3 controlled sets.
athleticMaintenance.tuesday: Aerobic session: 30–45 minutes at a conversational pace.
athleticMaintenance.wednesday: Upper-body strength: push, pull, overhead press, row and core carry; 3 sets.
athleticMaintenance.friday: Sport practice or 6 short efforts with full recovery; avoid all-out efforts if sore.
athleticMaintenance.saturday: Easy long session: 45–75 minutes walk, cycle or swim.
athleticMaintenance.sunday: Rest and prepare for the next week.

balancedActivity.title: Healthy range: balanced activity
balancedActivity.summary: Keep the habit broad: aerobic work, strength work and rest. This is general adult guidance, not a personal prescription.
balancedActivity.monday: 20–30 minute brisk walk; 2 sets of squats and wall push-ups.
balancedActivity.tuesday: 20–30 minute easy cycle or swim; 5 minute stretch.
balancedActivity.wednesday: Full-body strength: chair rise, row, step-up and plank; 2 sets of 10–12.
balancedActivity.thursday: Rest day or 15 minute gentle walk.
balancedActivity.friday: Brisk walk 30 minutes; add 3 short 20-second faster efforts if comfortable.
balancedActivity.saturday: Recreational activity you enjoy for 30–60 minutes.

bodyCompositionCheck.title: Higher BMI with athletic build: check body composition
bodyCompositionCheck.summary: Muscle can raise BMI. Do not assume the number means excess fat. Track waist, training performance and professional advice.
bodyCompositionCheck.monday: Keep strength training: lower-body session, 3 controlled sets.
bodyCompositionCheck.friday: Sport or intervals with full recovery; stop if joints hurt.
bodyCompositionCheck.saturday: Easy long session at a conversational pace.
bodyCompositionCheck.sunday: Rest. Consider discussing waist measurement or body-fat assessment with a professional.

gradualFatLoss.title: Overweight: gradual fat-loss routine
gradualFatLoss.summary: Aim for consistency and low joint impact. Build toward at least 150 minutes of moderate activity each week plus two strength days.
gradualFatLoss.monday: Brisk walk 30 minutes; 2 sets of chair rises, wall push-ups and band rows.
gradualFatLoss.tuesday: Easy walk 20–30 minutes and 10 minutes of mobility.
gradualFatLoss.wednesday: Strength: step-up, hip hinge, row and plank; 2 sets of 10–12.
gradualFatLoss.sunday: Rest. Choose water instead of sugary drinks and keep meals regular.

lowImpactFatLoss.title: Obesity category 1: low-impact, steady routine
lowImpactFatLoss.summary: Start below your limit and build slowly. Low-impact options protect joints while weekly activity increases.
lowImpactFatLoss.monday: Flat walk 15–20 minutes; seated marches and 2 sets of wall push-ups.
lowImpactFatLoss.wednesday: Chair-based strength: sit-to-stand, band row, heel raise and wall plank; 2 sets of 8–10.
lowImpactFatLoss.thursday: Easy walk or stationary cycling 20 minutes.
lowImpactFatLoss.friday: Repeat Wednesday with an extra set only if comfortable.
lowImpactFatLoss.saturday: Low-impact walk, cycle or water activity 20–30 minutes.
lowImpactFatLoss.sunday: Rest. Ask a professional if you have joint pain, breathlessness or chest discomfort.

medicalReviewFirst.title: Higher obesity category: medical review first
medicalReviewFirst.summary: Before increasing exercise, discuss safe options with a qualified healthcare professional, especially with joint pain, breathlessness, diabetes or heart symptoms.
medicalReviewFirst.monday: Gentle walk 10–15 minutes on flat ground, or chair mobility if walking is difficult.
medicalReviewFirst.wednesday: Seated strength: sit-to-stand, band row and heel raise; 1–2 easy sets.
medicalReviewFirst.thursday: Rest or short easy walk 10 minutes.
medicalReviewFirst.friday: Repeat Monday if you felt well; keep the pace conversational.
medicalReviewFirst.saturday: Gentle cycling or water movement 10–20 minutes if accessible.
medicalReviewFirst.sunday: Rest. Keep a symptom note to share with your clinician.
